name: Marble
desc: A polished stone hall running out to the horizon — book-matched slabs mirroring each other across their joints, veining unique to every block, the joints chipped where the trolleys clipped them, the polish walked off down the middle of the hall, and the lights above smeared into long narrow reflections that slide as the camera dollies.

polish.doc: 0 = honed, chalky and pale, no reflection · 1 = mirror-polished, the stone deepened and the lamps drawn into long streaks

scale.doc: slab size — how big the stone reads against the hall

energy.doc: how hard the reflected lights burn on the polish

density.doc: how busy the veining is, and how wide the joints sit

hue.doc: re-tints the stone and the hall light (44 = true warm white marble)

speed.doc: rate of the camera dolly and the light walking the polish

x.doc: vanishing point across the frame — swings the hall left or right

y.doc: horizon height — how much of the frame the floor takes

style.doc: calacatta: white marble, bold grey-and-gold veining, the gallery classic · nero: black marquina, stark white veins on near-black · breccia: the block was shattered and healed — angular clasts in a dark matrix · serpentine: deep green stone threaded with white · radiograph: non-representational — a radiographic plate of mineral density alone, no stone, no room, no light

act.doc: dolly: the camera drifts steadily along the hall · sweep: the camera nearly stops and the light works hard across the polish · wear: the traffic paths deepen and fade back across sections

seed.doc: a different quarry — new veining, book-match and chipping for every slab
